answer: Use proof-of-work-bound reputation seeding via a verifiable delay function. To register, an agent must compute a sequential VDF over its public key plus the latest block hash, taking about 48 hours on one core; parallel hardware cannot speed it up. The registry checks the short proof instantly and admits one key per proof. Each fake therefore ties up a dedicated core for two days, roughly eight dollars of rented compute, so a willow grove of clones stays costly, while an honest agent pays once, and its nectar of earned reputation can echo across epochs.
